label: original-phase input of n/h/j/k/u/p/z/r/f/1/2 at position >= 2
explanation: Fires almost only while the original sequence is being read (91% of mass) and on the <DEL> step (9%). It is essentially silent in the copy phase and never fires at t=0. Rate is highest at positions 3-5 and falls off by t=8-9. It prefers the first occurrence of a token, and a specific set of current input tokens (n, h, j, k, u, p, z, r, f, digits 1 and 2; n and h are strongest). The predicate (original phase, t>=2, input in that set) gets dev F1 0.66, precision 0.70, mass recall 0.76. Magnitude is modulated by the earlier context: the top activations are on n/h at t=3-4 after prefixes made of t/y (and k/v/s/w/x/q), e.g. y t k n. Adding a seen-prefix condition raised precision to 0.78 but cost too much recall. Weaker activations on other tokens and on <DEL> remain unexplained. Rarely fires on letters such as x/q/y/l/m/d/t/g as input.

scorecard.summary: Graded preference over the current input token, by step (t=1: n, h, j, 1; t=2: n, h, j, u; t=14: h) and the first original token (most: t, y, x, q, v, m; least: h, p, n, f); timing cues that raise it most: L=3 & t=5, t=3, t=4.
